---
title: "POLI 450A: Political Methodology I (Regression)"
subtitle: "Yiqing Xu, Stanford University"
---

Lecture slides, worksheets, R code and data for the first course in Stanford's political science
PhD methods sequence. The course covers point and interval estimation, hypothesis testing, simple
and multiple regression, and robust and clustered standard errors. The R scripts in the
[repository](https://github.com/xuyiqing/regression-lectures) draw the figures and print the
numbers on the slides from public data.

The slides have one page per slide. To present with the step-by-step
reveals, build that version from the LaTeX source. The worksheets are the in-class exercises. Each
lecture title opens the lecture's folder on GitHub: the LaTeX source, the figures, the R scripts
that draw them, and the data.

## Prerequisites

Linear algebra and calculus at the level of a political science math camp, and some
undergraduate probability, statistics and statistical computing. The course uses R.
